## Acceptance criteria — status, including one I am NOT ticking

- [x] **AC#1** met — `test_unregistered_parameterised_env_helper_aborts_the_scan`. The helper
  shape (`lookup_setting`) escapes BOTH pre-existing guards as the revised AC requires: not an
  `_llm_*`/`env_name` resolver in `llm/config.py`, and no `_SHIM_RE` match. Verified RED
  (`DID NOT RAISE RuntimeError`) before the fix existed, and returned to RED by mutation.
- [x] **AC#2** met — `test_dropping_a_used_helpers_row_fails_loudly_instead_of_shrinking`.
  Verified RED with the original loss: "silently after losing 4 variable(s)", naming the four
  b00f vars. The pre-existing b00f pins were NOT duplicated.
- [ ] **AC#3 — NOT ticked, deliberately.** Its first half is met: no false positives (`make
  lint` 0, `tests/unit` 11979 passed, `tests/scripts` 1048 passed). Its second half —
  "`docs/env-vars.md` does not change (162 keys)" — is **false, and could not have been true**.
  That clause encoded the assumption, reasonable when this ticket was filed, that the defect
  was prophylactic like its sibling 1979. The census disproved it: two keys were genuinely
  missing, so a correct fix MUST change the artifact (162 -> 164). Ticking this box would
  assert the fix found nothing. Recording the divergence instead of quietly re-interpreting
  the AC to fit the result.
- [ ] **AC#4 — not applicable.** It is the escape hatch for "if fail-closed is judged
  infeasible". It was judged FEASIBLE and implemented, so there is no infeasibility to record.
  The reasoning that got there — why the open-endedness objection dissolves under a dataflow
  predicate (9 hits / 557 files), and why the two rejected alternatives were rejected — is in
  the RCA comment, §6.

Gerrit 1990. Not closing until `Verified +1`.
